sentences.text: The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, praying to set aside the judgment and award dated 13.3.2015 in M.V.C. No.60 of 2013 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Gangavathi, and to allow the appeal filed by the claimant.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their rankings before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the claimant before the Tribunal are as under:
On 6.1.2013, the claimant was driving Tata Ace, bearing Registration No.KA-37/A-987, from Kalaburagi to Gangavathi and when the Tata Ace vehicle reached Lingasugur-Kalaburagi Road, near Golapalli Village at about 1:30 p.m., the driver of lorry, bearing Registration No.KA-29/3317, came from opposite direction in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Tata Ace vehicle.

Due to the said impact, the claimant and two NC: 2024:KHC-D:9847 other in-mates of the Tata Ace vehicle sustained injuries and hence, they were shifted to Hatti Government Hospital for treatment and thereafter, they were shifted to Government Hospital, Gangavathi.

4. Considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal granted compensation in respect of two other passengers in M.V.C. Nos.59 of 2013 and 61 of 2013, however, rejected the claim petition of the appellant in M.V.C. No.60 of 2013.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that the Tribunal committed an error in dismissing the claim petition filed by the claimant and the same is contrary to the documentary evidence and oral evidence adduced by the claimant.
Hence, he prays to allow the appeal.
6. Learned counsel for respondent No.4-Insurance Company has taken up the contention that the claimant has not at all sustained any injury.

As per the Wound NC: 2024:KHC-D:9847 Certificate,
he took treatment in private hospital and Ex.P5-Wound Certificate is created and concocted document in order to seek compensation from the Insurance Company.
Hence, he prayed to dismiss the appeal.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant, the learned counsel for respondent No.4 and perused the material available on record.
8.

Having heard the learned counsel for both parties, the point that arises for my consideration in this appeal is:

sentences.text:
Whether the appellant/claimant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry, bearing Registration No.KA-29/3317, and hence, he is entitled for compensation?
9.
From perusal of the evidence on record, it appears that on 6.1.2013 at 1:30 p.m., the driver of lorry caused the accident, hence, the petitioner and two others sustained injuries.
Thus, the claimant was shifted to NC: 2024:KHC-D:9847 Lingasugur Government Hospital for treatment, but the claimant has not furnished any Wound Certificate issued by the said Government Hospital.

Further,
the claimant, who was examined as PW2 has taken up the contention that he was treated at Gangavathi Government Hospital.
But, to substantiate This contention, the claimant has not furnished any Wound Certificate or Discharge Summary, to prove that, he has taken treatment at Gangavathi Government Hospital.
Admittedly, the claimant has relied upon Ex.P5-Wound Certificate which shows that the Certificate has been issued by private Doctor.

In the claim petition,
the claimant has not pleaded that, he has taken the treatment from private Hospitals.
These circumstances clearly establish that the claimant has not sustained any injury as contended by him and Ex.P5-Wound Certificate has been created for the purpose of claiming compensation.

Hence,
there is no merit in the appeal.
Considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal has rightly rejected the claim of the appellant.
Hence, no interference is called for in this appeal.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
In view of the dismissal of the appeal, I.A. No.1 of 2019 does not survive for consideration and accordingly, it is dismissed.
